title: Passive Cooling Technologies and Climate-Resilient Housing
subtitle: Vernacular architecture, high-albedo envelopes, radiative sky cooling, and thermal mass dynamics across the 21st century
description: A century-scale framework (2000–2100) arguing that low-cost passive cooling can make informal housing safer in extreme heat, organised around shade, ventilation, reflection and finance, in twelve chapters from cool roofs and radiative cooling to thermal mass, tenure and field trials.
contribution: A twelve-chapter monograph on passive cooling for informal housing, organised as four pillars (shade, ventilation, reflection and finance): the informal-housing heat penalty, cool roofs, radiative sky cooling, wind catchers, jaali screens, thermal mass, earth cooling, tenure and field trials, with a lexicon of its own terms.
abstract: Passive cooling is presented as a low-cost way to reduce heat exposure for residents of informal housing, where uninsulated metal roofs and dense layouts can push indoor temperatures well above outdoor air. The monograph organises passive measures into four pillars, shade, ventilation, reflection and finance, and argues that reflective roofs, radiative sky-cooling materials, wind catchers, perforated screens, thermal mass and earth cooling, together with tenure security and micro-finance, can protect residents without relying on air conditioning.

The monograph is organised in twelve chapters covering the informal housing heat penalty, the thermodynamics of heat rejection, cool roofs and coatings, passive daytime radiative cooling, stack ventilation and wind catchers, shading screens, thermal mass, sub-surface and evaporative cooling, tenure and governance, micro-retrofit finance and applied case studies from cities such as Ahmedabad, and closes with a century-scale synthesis across four planning periods from 2000 to 2100. It includes a lexicon of the framework’s defined terms.
coreProposition: Low-cost passive cooling, organised around shade, ventilation, reflection and finance, can protect residents of informal housing from extreme heat without depending on mechanical air conditioning.

keyFindings.title: The informal housing heat penalty.
keyFindings.text: The monograph argues that uninsulated corrugated metal roofs and dense layouts can make informal homes several degrees hotter inside than the air outside, affecting more than a billion people.

keyFindings.title: Reflect.
keyFindings.text: It argues that high-albedo coatings and cool roofs can sharply cut roof and ceiling temperatures at low cost, and that radiative sky-cooling materials can cool surfaces below the air temperature, even in sunlight.

keyFindings.title: Ventilate and shade.
keyFindings.text: It proposes wind catchers, solar chimneys and night ventilation, and perforated jaali and mashrabiya screens that block sun while accelerating breezes.

keyFindings.title: Thermal mass and earth cooling.
keyFindings.text: It argues that thick earth walls delay and damp heat, and that buried air tunnels and evaporative systems can chill incoming air without electricity.

keyFindings.title: Tenure and finance.
keyFindings.text: It argues that insecure tenure keeps households from investing in their homes, and proposes tenure agreements tied to retrofits and small revolving loans, utility on-bill repayment and carbon-offset income for micro-retrofits costing $50 to $150.

keyFindings.title: Field trials and a century in four periods.
keyFindings.text: It draws on pilots in Ahmedabad, Patna, Buenos Aires, Freetown and Cairo, and sets out a strategy through the informal heat crisis (2000–2025), standardized micro-retrofits (2025–2050), advanced metamaterials (2050–2075) and universal thermal security (2075–2100).

contents.title: The Informal Housing Heat Penalty: Urban Density and Thermal Inequality

The Vent Pillar: Buoyancy-Driven Stack Ventilation and Wind Catchers
The Shade Pillar: Vernacular Jaali Screens, Mashrabiya, and Vegetative Canopies

Sub-Surface and Evaporative Cooling: Earth-Air Heat Exchangers and Qanat Hydraulics

Applied Global Case Studies: Ahmedabad, Patna, Buenos Aires, Freetown, and Cairo

glossary.definition: The proactive application of economic development, technological diffusion, and institutional strengthening to reduce interconnected risks threatening human survivability.
The thermal disparity whereby informal settlements experience indoor temperatures 4°C to 8°C higher than ambient air due to uninsulated metallic roofs and dense morphology.
A proposed institutional elasticity metric quantifying the percentage of theoretically available climate adaptation capital that a household actually deploys into physical home thermal improvements.

A composite metric combining solar reflectance (albedo) and thermal emittance; cool roofs with SRI above 100 are described as rejecting over 85% of solar radiation, keeping indoor spaces up to 5.5°C cooler.

The capability of a surface to achieve sub-ambient temperatures under direct midday sunlight by simultaneously reflecting more than 96% of solar insolation and emitting strongly in the 8–13 µm atmospheric window.
The infrared spectral band between 8 and 13 micrometers where Earth’s atmosphere is largely transparent, allowing terrestrial thermal radiation to pass through into deep space.
The process wherein vertical air temperature gradients induce density differences, generating a continuous upward draft that exhausts warm air through rooftop apertures.
An ancient architectural tower rising above dense urban rooftops to capture faster, cooler upper boundary layer breezes, funneling them downward into living quarters across subterranean water basins.

A vertical thermal flue featuring a sun-exposed glazed face and dark absorber wall that superheats air to drive convective exhaust drafts (15–25 air changes per hour) even during windless summer afternoons.
The principle where airflow compressed through contracted apertures (such as jaali perforations) accelerates in velocity, stripping skin boundary layers to amplify physiological evaporative cooling.
Perforated stone, terracotta, or wooden architectural lattice screens that block high-angle direct solar radiation (up to 85%) while accelerating breezes and diffusing comfortable daylight indoors.
The time delay (measured in hours) for peak external surface heat to conduct through a building wall assembly to the inner surface; tuned to 10–12 hours in climate-resilient earth masonry.
The ratio of the interior surface temperature amplitude to the exterior ambient temperature amplitude; thick earth masonry is described as achieving μ below 0.20, dampening daily thermal extremes.

A high-density structural masonry block manufactured by subjecting subsoil mixtures to mechanical hydraulic compression (above 10 MPa), offering high thermal mass with 80% less carbon than fired brick.

A geothermal cooling system consisting of underground pipes that draw hot ambient air through subterranean soil at 2.5 m to 4 m depth, chilling the air by 8°C to 14°C before discharge into living spaces.
A proposed municipal covenant granting informal settlement residents immunity from eviction for 5 to 10 years conditioned upon the execution of verified passive cooling retrofits.
